# HEN MORNING ANALYSIS — 2026-08-18
**Hunt Energy Network | 32 BESS Sites | ERCOT**

---

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet RT average of **$49.27/MWh** represents a sharp escalation from the 3-day trend ($21.57 → $24.10 → $32.71), confirming an accelerating heat-driven demand response that is now materializing in real-time prices. **29 of 32 nodes** registered spike events (>$100/MWh), with the fleet peak hitting **$617.55/MWh** — the highest observed in the trailing 4-day window and a signal that locational congestion stress is intensifying across West and South Texas corridors. Nodes with negative DART (CISC_RN at RT exceeding DA by $22.67/MWh, MNWL_BESS_RN at $17.56/MWh, FRMRSVLW_RN at $13.97/MWh) were strong **RT outperformers** if dispatched in real-time — these nodes captured materially higher prices than the DA market offered, and should not be characterized as missed opportunities without confirming dispatch posture. On the DA-premium side, **POTEETS_RN** ($10.77 DA premium), **WLTC_ESR_RN** ($7.54), and **MV_VALV4_RN** ($7.37) successfully captured DA prices that exceeded RT settlement — favorable for any assets committed day-ahead. The simultaneous presence of three negative-price nodes (FALFUR_RN, PAVLOV_BT_RN, TYNAN_RN) alongside extreme spike nodes underscores deep intra-fleet price bifurcation driven by binding transmission constraints.

---

## 2. DISPATCH STRATEGY BY NODE

**🔵 LEAN DA — Commit Day-Ahead:**
- **PAVLOV_BT_RN** (Sharpe +0.217, avg DART +$2.20, MCC +$0.95/MWh): The strongest risk-adjusted DA signal in the fleet. Five-day history shows DA consistently premiums RT with manageable volatility ($10.11 stdev); the modest positive MCC is additive. Despite appearing on the negative-price node list yesterday, the 5-day Sharpe confirms DA commitment is the structurally superior posture — yesterday's RT dip was an anomaly, not a trend. **Recommend full DA commitment today.**
- **WLTC_ESR_RN** (Sharpe +0.172, avg DART +$1.16): DA premium is consistent but note the severely negative MCC of **-$268.39/MWh** — congestion is imposing a significant locational cost that partially offsets the DART advantage. The DA signal is intact but trading desk should flag this MCC drag as a CRR or hedging exposure that needs monitoring before scaling up commitment.

**🟡 LEAN RT — Prioritize Real-Time Dispatch:**
- **CISC_RN** (Sharpe -0.179, avg DART -$4.47, stdev $24.92, MCC +$26.09/MWh): RT has exceeded DA by an average of $4.47/MWh over 120 hours with a **positive MCC of +$26.09/MWh** — congestion is actively benefiting this node's RT position. This combination (consistent RT outperformance + congestion tailwind) makes CISC_RN the **highest-confidence RT dispatch candidate in the fleet today.** Avoid DA commitment; maximize RT energy offer flexibility.

**⚪ NEUTRAL — Monitor Closely:**
The 29-node neutral cohort spans the bulk of the fleet and reflects genuine dispatch uncertainty under volatile congestion conditions. Highest-priority monitoring targets within this group: **MNWL_BESS_RN** and **FRMRSVLW_RN** (both posted RT>DA by $17.56 and $13.97 respectively yesterday, and carry **positive MCCs of +$38.47 and +$38.27/MWh**) — if this RT outperformance pattern persists into today's price formation, these nodes may migrate toward LEAN_RT by tomorrow's Sharpe update and should be watched for intraday RT dispatch escalation.

---

- **PAVLOV_BT_RN & MAINLAND_RN** are the exposed nodes. Given the extreme shadow price and evening peak binding (HE21), assets on the load side of this constraint likely experienced significant locational depression or elevation depending on shift factor sign. With MAINLAND_RN in the neutral Sharpe cohort but exposed to a $1,350 avg shadow constraint, this is a **top-priority escalation item** — trading desk must confirm shift factor direction and whether CRR coverage exists.

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

The 7-day temperature forecast is uniformly extreme across all ERCOT regions, with **no meaningful cooling relief visible through August 24**. Wichita Falls hits **111°F today**, Abilene reaches **107°F by August 23**, DFW holds at **106–107°F all week**, and even coastal markets (Houston, Corpus Christi) remain at or above 99–101°F — all above seasonal norms that support ERCOT gross load sustained at or above the 89.1 GW baseline from August 17. Solar generation (34.9 GW yesterday) will continue to suppress midday RT prices across uncongested nodes, but the critical risk window remains **HE19–HE22** when solar ramps down into peak load — precisely the hours where yesterday's most severe constraints (MAGRUD, E_PASP, CARIZOSPG all peaking HE21) materialized. Precipitation probabilities are negligible statewide through August 22 (single digits for most markets, isolated 13–18% chances in Victoria and coastal areas that won't provide meaningful demand relief). **Trading desk implication:** Expect daily repeat of the HE20–22 spike pattern; pre-position BESS charge windows in HE10–14 solar trough pricing and target discharge at HE20–22 across the fleet, with particular focus on nodes where evening constraints are structurally favorable to RT prices.

---

The **Fort Duncan 2-Hr asset** is the standout performer at **$39,784/MW/yr**, exceeding its 2-Hr benchmark ($33,760/MW/yr) by $6,024/MW/yr, with energy_rtm of $26,130 (2x the benchmark's $12,930) confirming that FTDUNCAN_RN's RT-heavy dispatch posture and favorable congestion position are generating outsized value. The benchmark's top revenue streams (RRS_DAM at $4,033, energy_dam at $5,262) contrast sharply with HEN's reliance on energy_rtm and ECRS_DAM ($2,583) — suggesting HEN's edge is real-time price capture, not ancillary DA markets. As the summer heat regime drives RT volatility higher (fleet avg rising from $21.57 to $49.27 in 4 days), the **RT-heavy HEN strategy is entering its highest-value season**, and index outperformance should widen materially through August settlement.

---

**REGUP and RRS** have shown the most consistent DA premium over the trailing 3-day window, with both accelerating sharply on August 17 (REGUP: +$0.95/MW, RRS: +$1.03/MW) after near-flat readings on August 15–16 — the August 17 spike suggests DA buyers are beginning to price in evening reserve scarcity risk ahead of the heat dome peak. **HE23 is the single most actionable hour** across all AS services: REGUP HE23 averaged +$3.77/MW (peak $10.02 on Aug 17), RRS HE23 averaged +$3.60/MW (peak $9.89), NSPIN HE23 averaged +$9.59/MW (peak $16.94), and ECRS HE23 averaged +$6.02/MW (peak $16.36) — a remarkable convergence of DA premium across all reserve products in a single hour that reflects systematic RT reserve undersupply in the post-ramp period. **NSPIN carries the highest single-hour DA premium ($9.59 avg at HE23) but also the most dangerous RT risk: HE22 showed -$26.95/MW on August 17**, flagging a whipsaw pattern immediately preceding the peak hour — DA offers in NSPIN at HE22 carry material exposure. **Recommended priority for tomorrow's DA offer:** Concentrate REGUP and RRS DA offers at **HE22–HE24** where the 3-day DA premium is consistent, directional, and accelerating — avoid heavy NSPIN DA exposure at HE22 given the severe negative spread risk, and consider ECRS DA at HE23–HE24 as a secondary high-value target.
